name: SN-GCJA5 laser particulate matter sensor (I2C)
description: Panasonic laser-scattering PM sensor with I2C (address 0x33, fixed) and a UART TX output: reports PM1.0, PM2.5 and PM10 mass density (ug/m3, 0.001 resolution, +/-10 % from 35 to 1000 ug/m3) and particle counts in six size bins, refreshed every second. Runs from 5 V (+/-10 %, under 100 mA); its I2C and TX lines are 3.3 V logic with internal 10 kOhm pull-ups to the sensor's own 3.3 V. Sold as: SparkFun Particle Sensor - SN-GCJA5 (SPX-17123), 5-pin JST GH connector TX, SDA, SCL, GND, VDD (pin 1 to 5), wired with a JST GH 5-pin jumper cable.
eli5: A little fan pulls air past a laser and the sensor counts the dust and smoke specks, telling your board over two wires how dirty the air is.

pins.name: TX
pins.description: Pin 1: UART TX, 9600 baud 8E1, 3.3 V logic, one 32-byte frame per second. Not needed when using I2C; leave unconnected.

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: Pin 2: I2C data, 3.3 V logic, 10 kOhm pull-up inside the sensor to its own 3.3 V (no external pull-up needed)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: Pin 3: I2C clock, 3.3 V logic, 10 kOhm pull-up inside the sensor to its own 3.3 V

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Pin 4: Ground (the metal shell is also tied to GND)

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Pin 5: Supply 5 V +/-10 % (4.5-5.5 V), under 100 mA. Feed it from the board's 5V/VBUS pin, not 3V3.

buildNotes: Power VDD from 5 V (the board's 5V/VBUS pin); the sensor makes its own 3.3 V, and SDA/SCL/TX are 3.3 V logic, so they connect straight to an ESP32 or Pico.
The sensor already has 10 kOhm pull-ups on SDA and SCL to its internal 3.3 V. Do not add pull-ups to 5 V.
I2C address 0x33 (fixed), up to 400 kHz. Multi-byte values are little-endian: PM registers 0x00/0x04/0x08 are 4 bytes each, value / 1000 = ug/m3.
Registers update once per second. The first reading comes about 8 s after power-up and readings settle after about 28 s; STATE (0x26) fan bits read 2 during initial calibration.
Connector is a JST GH 5-pin (SM05B-GHS-TB); pin 1 is TX, pin 5 is VDD. Use a GH-to-jumper cable and check the colours against the pin numbers.
Keep the air inlet and outlet clear and out of strong drafts; do not short the grounded metal shell to anything but GND.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from sn_gcja5 import SNGCJA5

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
sensor = SNGCJA5(i2c)
while True:
    try:
        pm1, pm25, pm10 = sensor.pm()
        print('PM1=%.1f PM2.5=%.1f PM10=%.1f ug/m3' % (pm1, pm25, pm10))
    except OSError as e:
        print('waiting for sensor:', e)
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Reports the PM1.0, PM2.5 and PM10 set on the sliders

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading. Not yet tested on real hardware.
